publicContract.disabledContract: Disabled tabs remain focusable by arrow navigation but refuse activation; do not apply Select skip semantics.

criteria: Blank external scaffold contains no Tabs solution; old versions, tarball and installed d000174e skills bytes are reused.

Architecture review confirms standalone AppTabs composes RdxTabsRoot on its host via hostDirectives, renders RdxTabsList in its own template before the projected panels and accepts the consumer's tab/panel parts.
Both generated consumer and independent parent compile with strictTemplates against public package imports, without workspace aliases or source inputs.

Projected parts resolve Root/List DI ownership; each list is named; tabs have unique ids and linked aria-controls, and corresponding panels have reciprocal ids/aria-labelledby. Exactly one panel is visible per instance.
Manual ArrowRight/Left and Home/End move focus without activation; Enter/Space activate the focused enabled tab with expected value/reason and no duplicate callbacks.
The middle disabled Billing tab receives arrow focus but Enter, Space and a real pointer attempt do not activate it or emit changes.
External selected-value updates render without emitting user change callbacks; ids remain stable through value changes.
Two simultaneous instances use the same account/billing/security values but retain independent selection, callback counts, ids, tab/panel associations and focus.
Tab leaves the list for the active panel; reverse navigation returns to its selected tab, using the established macOS WebKit keyboard convention.
Six scenarios per host, two hosts, three engines: 36 cases, fresh contexts, no retries, traces for every result, and pageerror/console collection before navigation.
rules: Freeze prompt, public contract, independent parent and checks before live generation.
